To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the accuracy with which conformal treatment plans are calculated can be determined by comparing the calculated with the measured dose in the high-isodose region.

(1) the 95% dose level is a good choice for the prescribed dose level in a multi-field irradiation technique, because of its steep dose gradients, and because it can easily be verified by a set of water scans, and (2) the 95%-level plus or minus its standard deviation can be used to indicate the accuracy with which a conformal treatment plan is realized.

(i) the uncertainty in the 95% dose surface is not constant, but is related to the local dose gradient and (ii) the 95% surface can therefore not be represented by a single isodose line of constant width.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the verification of the 3-D dose distributions in the high-doseregion for a specific conformal multi-field irradiation technique.
the verification of the 3-D dose calculation in the high-doseregion.
the accuracy of the calculated 90-100% isodose surfaces in conformal treatment plans, which are important for the quality assurance of the dose distribution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the calculated 95%-isodose surface is accurate within 3 mm for this specific technique, which is in agreement with the results of the commissioning of the treatment planning system.
the 95% dose surface is calculated with an uncertainty of 2 mm, which is a value that is acceptable for clinical use.
the accuracy with which conformal irradiation techniques can be planned and delivered is limited by the uncertainty in the calculation of the high-dose isodoses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the accuracy of the 3-D dose distribution in the high-doseregion of a conformal irradiated phantom can be assessed by a combination of water phantom scans and a reconstruction method.
the accuracy of the calculated 3-D dose distribution in the high-doseregion is determined by a combination of the dose accuracy and the spatial resolution.
the 95% confidence level of the calculated isodose surface should not exceed the prescribed isodense surface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the accuracy of the 95th isodose position depends on the dose gradient in the high-dosage region, and the accuracy of the calculated isodoses can be indicated as a confidence region.
the accuracy with which an isodose surface of the treatment plan is realized is not constant over the whole volume of the target.
the accuracy with which treatment plans are calculated can be assessed by measuring the 95% high-dose region in water.
